_comment: Hand-authored dispute cases. Not generated, not sampled from a simulator -- Lane 2 is deliberately thin and these nine cases exist to exercise every branch of the evidence engine: a clear contest, a clear abandon, a blocking gap, an EV-negative win, and the Lane 1 overlap. Amounts are integer paise.

cases.merchantNote: Annual SaaS plan. Customer says they cancelled in-app before the renewal debit.
cases.truth: Cancellation was submitted four days AFTER the debit. The merchant is in the right and the record proves it.

cases.merchantNote: OTT subscription. Customer cancelled, then was billed the next cycle.
cases.truth: The cancellation record is missing because support handled it over the phone and never logged it. The customer is probably right.

cases.merchantNote: Card-absent fraud claim on a first-time high-value order.
cases.truth: No 3DS authentication record. Liability never shifted, so this cannot be won.

cases.merchantNote: Customer says they were charged twice on the same day.
cases.truth: Two genuinely distinct orders placed 40 minutes apart, different line items. Highly winnable.

cases.merchantNote: Digital course purchase; customer says they never got access.
cases.truth: Delivery proof is mandatory and absent. Usage logs show two logins, but without fulfilment confirmation the packet is incomplete.

cases.merchantNote: Refund was approved but the customer disputed before it settled.
cases.truth: Complete evidence, but the amount is small enough that filing costs more than the expected recovery.

cases.merchantNote: Insurance premium debited after the customer says they lapsed the policy.
cases.truth: Full packet. The mandate was live and no cancellation was received before the debit.

cases.merchantNote: Cardholder does not recognise a recurring SaaS charge.
cases.truth: Eleven prior undisputed debits on the same card and device. Almost certainly friendly fraud, and the history shows it.

cases.merchantNote: Customer says the delivered product did not match the listing.
cases.truth: Thin packet on an inherently subjective code. Winnable in principle, marginal in practice.
